puhap1.q: Vancomycin is primarily used in nosocomial pneumonia to cover which pathogen?
opts: Correct. Vancomycin is primarily used for empiric coverage of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, the most common gram-positive cause of nosocomial pneumonia.
Pseudomonas is covered by the antipseudomonal beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones and aminoglycosides; vancomycin is for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
The atypicals are covered by the fluoroquinolones; vancomycin is primarily for empiric methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage.
Aspergillus is a fungal pathogen of nosocomial pneumonia and vancomycin is an antibacterial; its use is methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage.

puhap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which drug is a limited-spectrum empiric choice for nosocomial pneumonia without multidrug-resistant risk factors?
opts: Cefepime is an antipseudomonal cephalosporin, part of broad-spectrum coverage for multidrug-resistant risk; ceftriaxone is the limited-spectrum cephalosporin.
Meropenem is an antipseudomonal carbapenem used for broad coverage; the limited-spectrum carbapenem is ertapenem.
Vancomycin is the gram-positive add-on in broad-spectrum coverage; without multidrug-resistant risk factors, a limited agent such as ceftriaxone is used.
Correct. Limited-spectrum coverage is ceftriaxone, or levofloxacin or moxifloxacin, or ampicillin-sulbactam, or ertapenem.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Why should fluoroquinolones be used judiciously in nosocomial pneumonia?
opts: Fluoroquinolones have good lung tissue penetration; the reason for judicious use is increasing gram-negative resistance.
Fluoroquinolones have good activity against the atypicals; the reason for judicious use is rising gram-negative resistance.
The antipseudomonal fluoroquinolones do require renal adjustment; the reason for judicious use is rising gram-negative resistance.
Correct. Increasing use of fluoroquinolones is leading to gram-negative resistance, so they should be used judiciously.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A proposed empiric regimen for nosocomial pneumonia with multidrug-resistant risk factors is cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin. What makes it inappropriate?
opts: Vancomycin is in the regimen and is the usual methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) coverage; the flaw is two beta-lactams together.
ruled out by a stated finding
It has no antipseudomonal drug in it
Cefepime and piperacillin-tazobactam are both antipseudomonal; the problem is that both are beta-lactams, so a fluoroquinolone or aminoglycoside is missing.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Cefepime and piperacillin-tazobactam are both antipseudomonal beta-lactams; the partner must be an antipseudomonal fluoroquinolone or an aminoglycoside.
It needs linezolid in place of vancomycin
Vancomycin or linezolid is equally acceptable as the gram-positive drug; the regimen fails because it pairs two beta-lactams.

puhap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which gram-negative bacillus is the most common cause of nosocomial pneumonia?
opts: Escherichia coli is on the gram-negative list, but Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the most common gram-negative cause.

Correct. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the most common gram-negative bacillus, followed by Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter, Enterobacter and Serratia; methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is the most common gram-positive coccus.
Klebsiella pneumoniae is listed among the gram-negative bacilli, but Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the most common.
Acinetobacter is a listed gram-negative bacillus, but the most common gram-negative cause is Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

puhap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A hospitalized patient carries several risks for pneumonia. Which of them is one that cannot be changed?
opts: Correct. Unmodifiable risk factors are age over 70, chronic lung disease, depressed consciousness, large-volume aspiration and hospitalization during the winter months.
Histamine H2 blocker or antacid therapy is a modifiable risk factor, since the therapy can be changed.
Reintubation is listed among the modifiable risk factors, with mechanical ventilation and a nasogastric tube.
An intracranial pressure monitor is a modifiable risk factor; hospitalization during the winter months is unmodifiable.

puhap1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which drawback is listed for linezolid?
opts: Linezolid is available in both intravenous and oral forms; its listed drawback is that it is expensive.
Linezolid has good lung penetration; poor penetration is the aminoglycoside problem. Linezolid's drawback is cost.
Linezolid needs no dose adjustment for renal function; its listed drawback is that it is expensive.
Correct. Linezolid is expensive, though it has great methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage, oral and intravenous forms, good lung penetration and no renal adjustment.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Why is ceftazidime rarely used as the antipseudomonal cephalosporin for nosocomial pneumonia?
opts: Seizure caution is stated for imipenem-cilastatin, a carbapenem; ceftazidime is set aside because resistance develops rapidly.
Limited Pseudomonas activity describes ertapenem; ceftazidime is antipseudomonal, but resistance to it develops rapidly.
Both antipseudomonal cephalosporins require renal adjustment; ceftazidime's problem is rapid development of resistance.
Correct. Ceftazidime (Fortaz) is not recommended because of rapid development of resistance and is rarely used; cefepime is the choice.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A proposed empiric regimen for nosocomial pneumonia with multidrug-resistant risk factors is vancomycin, linezolid and tobramycin. What makes it inappropriate?
opts: The reverse: vancomycin and linezolid are both gram-positive coverage, one too many; the regimen needs a second gram-negative agent instead.
It has only one gram-negative agent
Correct. Vancomycin and linezolid both cover methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), so only tobramycin covers gram-negative organisms; two are needed.
None of these three is a beta-lactam: vancomycin and linezolid are the two gram-positive drugs, and tobramycin is an aminoglycoside.
An aminoglycoside such as tobramycin is a listed second gram-negative agent; the flaw is that only one gram-negative drug is present.

puhap1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A patient with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia is ready to finish therapy at home by mouth. Which drug allows this?
opts: Correct. Linezolid has great methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage and comes in intravenous and oral forms, with good lung penetration.
Vancomycin covers methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, but the agent named with both intravenous and oral forms for pneumonia is linezolid.
ruled out by a stated finding
Tobramycin is an aminoglycoside second gram-negative agent, not methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage; linezolid is the oral option.
Cefepime is an antipseudomonal cephalosporin and does not cover methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus; linezolid does, by mouth.

puhap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A patient admitted for a hip fracture develops a new pneumonia on hospital day 4; it was not present on admission. How is this pneumonia classified?
opts: Pneumonia that was not present at admission and begins more than 48 hours into the stay is nosocomial, not community-acquired.
ruled out by a stated finding
Ventilator-associated pneumonia is one nosocomial type, but nothing in this case involves mechanical ventilation; this is hospital-acquired pneumonia.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Nosocomial pneumonia is a lung infection not present at admission and occurring more than 48 hours after admission; it includes hospital-acquired pneumonia.
Acute bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchi that spares the bronchioles and alveoli; a new pneumonia after 48 hours in hospital is nosocomial.

puhap1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which property of aminoglycosides is the reason for extended-interval (once daily or longer) dosing in pneumonia?
opts: The reverse: aminoglycosides penetrate the lung poorly, which is why bigger doses giving higher concentrations are used.
Aminoglycosides are nephrotoxic and ototoxic and highly dependent on renal function; extended intervals answer their poor lung penetration.
Correct. Aminoglycosides penetrate the lung poorly, so bigger, less frequent doses give the higher concentrations needed.
Good activity against atypicals belongs to the fluoroquinolones; aminoglycoside dosing reflects their poor lung penetration.

puhap1.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which drug's use is a modifiable risk factor for nosocomial pneumonia?
opts: Correct. Histamine H2 blocker or antacid therapy is a modifiable risk factor for nosocomial pneumonia, and famotidine is a histamine H2 blocker.
Albuterol, a beta-2 agonist bronchodilator, is not on the risk list; the drug therapies listed are histamine H2 blockers or antacids and previous antibiotics.
Montelukast, a leukotriene receptor antagonist, is not a listed risk factor; histamine H2 blockers such as famotidine are.
Cromolyn, a mast cell stabilizer, is not a listed risk factor; histamine H2 blocker or antacid therapy is.

puhap1.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which statement about meropenem, compared with imipenem-cilastatin, is correct?
opts: The antipseudomonal carbapenems require renal adjustment; meropenem's difference from imipenem is its lower seizure risk.
Correct. Meropenem (Merrem) carries less risk for seizures than imipenem-cilastatin, which is used with caution in patients with a seizure history.
Limited activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa describes ertapenem; meropenem is an antipseudomonal carbapenem with less seizure risk.
Cefepime is the fourth-generation cephalosporin; meropenem is a carbapenem, distinguished by its lower seizure risk.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A patient develops hospital-acquired pneumonia on hospital day 7 and has no other risk factors for multidrug-resistant pathogens. Which initial approach fits?
opts: Limited-spectrum therapy requires both early onset and no multidrug-resistant risk factors; onset on day 7 is late.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Late onset, 5 days or more, is enough on its own to call for broad-spectrum initial antibiotic therapy for multidrug-resistant pathogens.
Therapy starts as soon as possible without waiting on a culture, and late onset calls for broad-spectrum coverage.
Supportive care alone is the approach to acute bronchitis; late-onset hospital-acquired pneumonia needs broad-spectrum antibiotics.

puhap1.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which antipseudomonal agent is a penicillin combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor?
opts: Ampicillin-sulbactam is a penicillin with a beta-lactamase inhibitor, but it is a limited-spectrum option, not an antipseudomonal agent.
Imipenem-cilastatin is an antipseudomonal carbapenem, not a penicillin with a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is an outpatient community-acquired pneumonia beta-lactam, not an antipseudomonal agent.
Correct. Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn) is the antipseudomonal penicillin with a beta-lactamase inhibitor, and it requires renal adjustment.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: A patient fails therapy for nosocomial pneumonia and is found to have a pulmonary embolus. Which category of treatment failure is this?
opts: Correct. A pulmonary embolus or a neoplasm is a wrong-diagnosis failure; resistant pathogens are wrong therapy, and Clostridioides difficile colitis, empyema or lung abscess are complications.
Wrong therapy means resistant pathogens or inadequate antimicrobial therapy; a pulmonary embolus means the diagnosis was wrong.
Complications are Clostridioides difficile colitis, empyema or lung abscess; a pulmonary embolus is a wrong-diagnosis failure.
Drug toxicity is not one of the failure categories; a pulmonary embolus found on workup is a wrong diagnosis.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: When is a vancomycin trough level drawn?
opts: There is no trough before any drug has been given; the vancomycin trough is drawn prior to the third or fourth dose, at steady state.
Before the third or fourth dose
Correct. The trough is drawn prior to the third to fourth dose, when vancomycin is at steady state.
A level right after the first dose is neither a trough nor at steady state; the trough is drawn before the third or fourth dose.
At the end of the course
Waiting until the end of therapy defeats the purpose; the trough is drawn before the third or fourth dose, at steady state.

puhap1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: What should happen to empiric nosocomial pneumonia therapy once cultures and sensitivities return?
opts: Broad empiric coverage is meant to be streamlined; once cultures and sensitivities are available, coverage is scaled back.
Candida and Aspergillus are listed pathogens, but the rule when cultures return is to streamline therapy, not broaden it.
Narrow it to the culture results
Correct. Therapy is streamlined once cultures and sensitivities are available, scaling back antibiotic coverage as the cultures return.
Vancomycin or linezolid is the single gram-positive agent in broad coverage; when cultures return, therapy is streamlined.

puhap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: Which risk factor for nosocomial pneumonia is modifiable?
opts: Chronic lung disease is listed as an unmodifiable risk factor, along with age over 70 and depressed consciousness.
Age over 70 is an unmodifiable risk factor; a nasogastric tube is one of the modifiable ones.
Correct. Modifiable risk factors are mechanical ventilation, a nasogastric tube, an intracranial pressure monitor, histamine H2 blocker or antacid therapy, previous antibiotics and reintubation.
Depressed consciousness is listed as unmodifiable; the modifiable list includes devices such as a nasogastric tube.

puhap1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap1.q: For broad-spectrum empiric coverage of nosocomial pneumonia, which drugs supply the gram-positive coverage added to the gram-negative combination?
opts: Ceftriaxone and ertapenem are limited-spectrum options for patients without multidrug-resistant risk; the gram-positive add-on is vancomycin or linezolid.
Correct. Broad coverage is gram-negative combination therapy plus gram-positive coverage with vancomycin or linezolid, for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
Aminoglycosides are a second gram-negative agent in the combination, not the gram-positive coverage, which is vancomycin or linezolid.
Azithromycin or doxycycline partners a beta-lactam in community-acquired pneumonia; the nosocomial gram-positive add-on is vancomycin or linezolid.

puhap2.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Why is ertapenem a limited-spectrum choice rather than a broad one in nosocomial pneumonia?
opts: Rapid development of resistance is the concern raised about ceftazidime, not ertapenem; ertapenem is limited by weak Pseudomonas activity.
Poor lung penetration is the aminoglycoside problem; ertapenem is limited-spectrum because of its weak activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Correct. Ertapenem is a narrow-spectrum carbapenem with limited activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, so it belongs to limited-spectrum coverage.
Seizure caution belongs to imipenem-cilastatin; ertapenem is limited-spectrum because of its weak activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

puhap2.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which cephalosporin is a fourth-generation antipseudomonal agent?
opts: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin used in community-acquired pneumonia and limited-spectrum nosocomial coverage, not an antipseudomonal agent.
Cefuroxime is a second- or third-generation cephalosporin for outpatient community-acquired pneumonia; cefepime is the fourth-generation antipseudomonal one.
Cefotaxime is an intravenous beta-lactam for ward community-acquired pneumonia; the fourth-generation antipseudomonal cephalosporin is cefepime.
Correct. Cefepime (Maxipime) is a fourth-generation antipseudomonal cephalosporin, and, like ceftazidime, it requires renal adjustment.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: In broad-spectrum coverage, an antipseudomonal beta-lactam is paired with which second gram-negative agent?
opts: Moxifloxacin is listed in the limited-spectrum group; the antipseudomonal fluoroquinolones for the combination are levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin.
Correct. The antipseudomonal beta-lactam is combined with an antipseudomonal fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin or ciprofloxacin) or an aminoglycoside.
Ceftriaxone is a limited-spectrum cephalosporin, not an antipseudomonal partner; the second gram-negative agent is an antipseudomonal fluoroquinolone or an aminoglycoside.
Linezolid is gram-positive coverage for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, not a second gram-negative agent.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which regimen fits broad-spectrum empiric coverage for nosocomial pneumonia with risk factors for multidrug-resistant pathogens?
opts: This covers gram-negative organisms twice but leaves out the gram-positive agent, vancomycin or linezolid, that broad coverage requires.
ruled out by a stated finding
A beta-lactam plus a macrolide is community-acquired pneumonia treatment; it lacks antipseudomonal and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage.
Correct. Broad coverage is an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime) plus an antipseudomonal fluoroquinolone or aminoglycoside (tobramycin) plus vancomycin or linezolid.
Ertapenem has limited Pseudomonas activity, so it cannot be the antipseudomonal beta-lactam of a broad regimen.
ruled out by a stated finding

puhap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: What do cefepime and ceftazidime both require?
opts: Seizure caution is stated for imipenem-cilastatin, not the antipseudomonal cephalosporins, which both require renal adjustment.
Trough levels belong to vancomycin, drawn before the third or fourth dose; cefepime and ceftazidime both require renal adjustment.
Correct. Both antipseudomonal cephalosporins require renal adjustment, as do the antipseudomonal carbapenems, penicillins and fluoroquinolones.
No hepatic adjustment is stated for the antipseudomonal cephalosporins; both require renal adjustment.

puhap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: A patient develops hospital-acquired pneumonia on hospital day 3 and has no risk factors for multidrug-resistant pathogens. Which initial approach fits?
opts: Broad-spectrum therapy for multidrug-resistant pathogens is for late onset (5 days or more) or multidrug-resistant risk factors, neither present here.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. With early onset (under 5 days) and no multidrug-resistant risk factors, limited-spectrum initial antibiotic therapy is chosen.
Treatment is not delayed for a culture: therapy starts as soon as possible, here with limited-spectrum antibiotics.
Supportive care alone is for acute bronchitis; hospital-acquired pneumonia is treated at once, here with limited-spectrum therapy.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Besides Pseudomonas, the antipseudomonal fluoroquinolones have good activity against which group of pathogens?
opts: Correct. Ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin have good activity against the atypicals (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Legionella) and good lung tissue penetration.
Candida and Aspergillus fumigatus are fungal causes of nosocomial pneumonia, not organisms the fluoroquinolones cover; their strength is the atypicals.
Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is covered by vancomycin or linezolid; the fluoroquinolones have good activity against the atypicals.
Anaerobes are not named for the fluoroquinolones; the stated strength is good activity against the atypicals Mycoplasma, Chlamydia and Legionella.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which history meets a listed criterion for health-care associated pneumonia?
opts: Wound care counts only within the previous 30 days; six months ago falls outside the criterion.
A hospital stay counts when it was more than 2 days in an acute care facility within the past 90 days, not a year ago.

Correct. Health-care associated pneumonia criteria include hemodialysis, nursing home residence, recent intravenous antibiotics, chemotherapy, wound care in the previous 30 days and a recent hospital stay.
A child in day care at home
Exposure to a child in day care is a risk factor for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, not a health-care associated pneumonia criterion.

puhap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: When should antibiotic therapy for suspected nosocomial pneumonia begin?
opts: Waiting is exactly what is advised against: therapy starts as soon as possible, without waiting on a definitive culture.
A gram stain is not a gate to treatment; therapy for nosocomial pneumonia starts as soon as possible.
Forty-eight hours after admission defines nosocomial pneumonia; once it is suspected, therapy starts as soon as possible.
Correct. Therapy starts as soon as possible, without waiting on a definitive culture, with broad-spectrum antibiotics that consider multidrug-resistant pathogens.

puhap2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which finding is listed as a complication that causes failure of pneumonia therapy?
opts: A neoplasm is a wrong-diagnosis failure, not a complication; the complications are Clostridioides difficile colitis, empyema and lung abscess.
A pulmonary embolus is a wrong-diagnosis failure; the listed complications are Clostridioides difficile colitis, empyema and lung abscess.
Resistant pathogens are a wrong-therapy failure; the listed complications are Clostridioides difficile colitis, empyema and lung abscess.
Correct. Complications causing failure are Clostridioides difficile colitis, empyema or lung abscess; a pulmonary embolus or neoplasm is a wrong diagnosis.

puhap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Why is a patient switched to oral antibiotics when possible during pneumonia treatment?
opts: Lung penetration depends on the drug, not the route; the stated reason to switch to oral therapy is that it is cheaper.
Coverage is scaled back, not broadened, as cultures return; the reason for the oral switch is that it is cheaper.
Correct. Antibiotics are switched to oral when or if possible because oral therapy is cheaper, as coverage is scaled back to the culture results.
Resistance is not the stated reason; the switch to oral therapy when possible is made because it is cheaper.

puhap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which history counts as a risk factor for multidrug-resistant pathogens in hospital-acquired pneumonia?
opts: Correct. Risk factors for multidrug-resistant pathogens are prior antibiotics, colonization, hospitalization or chronic care, and immunosuppressive disease or therapy.
Winter hospitalization is an unmodifiable risk factor for nosocomial pneumonia itself, not a listed risk factor for multidrug-resistant pathogens.
Depressed consciousness raises the risk of nosocomial pneumonia, but it is not among the multidrug-resistant risk factors in the algorithm.
Large-volume aspiration is an unmodifiable risk factor for nosocomial pneumonia, not one of the multidrug-resistant risk factors.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which hospitalized group has a higher incidence of nosocomial pneumonia?
opts: Youth is not a stated risk; the groups with higher incidence are the elderly and mechanically ventilated patients.
Recent bronchitis is not a listed risk; the higher incidence is in elderly and mechanically ventilated patients.
Nosocomial pneumonia arises more than 48 hours after admission, so a stay under a day is not a risk group; the higher incidence is in elderly and mechanically ventilated patients.
Correct. Nosocomial pneumonia has a higher incidence in elderly and mechanically ventilated patients, with higher mortality and hospital costs.

puhap2.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which drug is an aminoglycoside?
opts: Correct. The aminoglycosides are gentamicin, tobramycin and amikacin, used as a second gram-negative agent in broad coverage.
Azithromycin is a macrolide used in community-acquired pneumonia, not an aminoglycoside like gentamicin, tobramycin and amikacin.
Ampicillin is a penicillin beta-lactam; the aminoglycosides are gentamicin, tobramycin and amikacin.
Ertapenem is a narrow-spectrum carbapenem; the aminoglycosides are gentamicin, tobramycin and amikacin.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: How does nosocomial pneumonia rank among infections in hospitalized patients?
opts: First, ahead of urinary tract infection
Urinary tract infection is the more common one; nosocomial pneumonia ranks second, after it.
Correct. Nosocomial pneumonia is the second most common infection in hospitalized patients, after urinary tract infection, with higher mortality and costs.
Wound infection is not the comparison given; nosocomial pneumonia is second most common, after urinary tract infection.
Third, after urinary and wound infection
Nosocomial pneumonia ranks second, not third; the only infection more common in hospitalized patients is urinary tract infection.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: A patient on a ventilator develops pneumonia and has risk factors for multidrug-resistant pathogens. Which empiric regimen is appropriate?
opts: Correct. Meropenem is an antipseudomonal carbapenem, gentamicin an aminoglycoside as the second gram-negative agent, and linezolid the gram-positive coverage.
Imipenem-cilastatin and cefepime are both antipseudomonal beta-lactams; the second gram-negative agent must be a fluoroquinolone or an aminoglycoside.
Vancomycin and linezolid both cover methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), leaving one gram-negative agent where two are needed.
ruled out by a stated finding
Ceftriaxone is a limited-spectrum third-generation cephalosporin, not antipseudomonal; the beta-lactam must be antipseudomonal.

puhap2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: On what are aminoglycoside dose and frequency adjusted?
opts: Correct. Aminoglycoside dose and frequency are adjusted based on levels, and they are highly dependent on renal function.
No hepatic basis is given; aminoglycoside dosing is adjusted on drug levels and depends heavily on renal function.
The sputum gram stain is a controversial diagnostic test, not a dosing guide; aminoglycosides are adjusted on measured levels.
The white blood cell count does not set the dose; aminoglycoside dose and frequency are adjusted on measured levels.

puhap2.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which antipseudomonal agent is used with caution in a patient with a seizure history?
opts: Meropenem is the carbapenem with less seizure risk; the caution for a seizure history is attached to imipenem-cilastatin.
Correct. Imipenem-cilastatin (Primaxin) is used with caution in patients with a seizure history; meropenem carries less seizure risk.
Piperacillin-tazobactam carries a renal-adjustment note, not a seizure caution; imipenem-cilastatin is the agent used with caution in seizure history.
Tobramycin's listed toxicities are ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity; the seizure caution belongs to imipenem-cilastatin.

puhap2.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: Which drug used for nosocomial pneumonia needs no dose adjustment for renal function?
opts: Vancomycin requires renal adjustment and is nephrotoxic with other nephrotoxins; linezolid needs no renal dose adjustment.
Correct. Linezolid (Zyvox) needs no dose adjustment based on renal function; vancomycin, the aminoglycosides and the antipseudomonal beta-lactams all require renal adjustment.
Tobramycin, an aminoglycoside, is highly dependent on renal function; linezolid is the drug with no renal dose adjustment.
Cefepime requires renal adjustment like the other antipseudomonal cephalosporin; linezolid needs none.

puhap2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
puhap2.q: In limited-spectrum coverage for nosocomial pneumonia, which drug is chosen when atypical pathogens are a concern?
opts: Ceftriaxone is a limited-spectrum option, but the group to choose when atypical pathogens are a worry is levofloxacin or moxifloxacin.
Ampicillin-sulbactam is a limited-spectrum option, but the fluoroquinolones are the group chosen for atypical pathogens.
Ertapenem is a narrow-spectrum carbapenem option; when atypical pathogens are a worry, levofloxacin or moxifloxacin is chosen.
Correct. Levofloxacin or moxifloxacin is the limited-spectrum choice when atypical pathogens are a worry; fluoroquinolones have good activity against Mycoplasma, Chlamydia and Legionella.

puhap2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
puhap2.q: Which two toxicities are listed for the aminoglycosides?
opts: Hepatitis and hyperuricemia are pyrazinamide's adverse effects; aminoglycosides cause ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
Peripheral neuritis and a lupus-like syndrome are isoniazid's adverse effects; aminoglycosides cause ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
Correct. Aminoglycosides cause ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, and their dosing is highly dependent on renal function.
Seizures and arrhythmias are the toxic effects of high theophylline levels; aminoglycosides cause ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
